questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Amman?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Jordan is Amman.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Jordan about 89,341 square kilometres; Armenia about 29,743 square kilometres; Israel about 20,770 square kilometres; Qatar about 11,437 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Jordan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: The capital of Jordan is Amman.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Jordan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Jordan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Jordan article.

questions.proof: Natural borders that separate it from its Arab neighbors are the Jordan River, which separates Jordan and Israel as well as the Yarmouk River, which separates Jordan and Syria.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Jordan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Jordan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
